Tinku @ Md. Asif vs The State Of West Bengal on 6 January,
2026
Author: Rajasekhar Mantha

Bench: Rajasekhar Mantha
 6.
06.01.2026.
 ap
 I.A. No. Cran 1 of 2025

In
 C.R.A. 410 of 2012
 Tinku @ Md. Asif
 Versus
 The State of West Bengal
 Mr. Soumyajit Das Mahapatra,
 Mr. Kunal Ganguly,
 Mr. Ankit Mukherjee,
 Ms. Upasana Banerjee. ...
For the appellant.

Mr. Prasun Kumar Dutta,
 Mr. Binoy Kumar Panda.
.... For the State.

Re: CRAN 1 of 2025  1.
This Court has considered the report of the Superintendent, Asansol District Correctional Home dated 14th December, 2025.
The same is taken on record.

2. In a sessions trial, the appellant was convicted under Sections 304B/498A of the Indian Penal Code by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Asansol, Burdwan and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life for the offences punishable under Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/-
and in default thereof, suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months for the offences punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Asansol, Burdwan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Against such order of conviction and sentence, a statutory appeal has been preferred by the appellant which has already been admitted.
Now, with the liberty granted by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court admitting the appeal, the appellant has approached this Court for suspension of sentence.

entities.text: Tinku @ Md. Asif vs The State Of West Bengal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The appellant is stated to have undergone 17 years 7 days of incarceration as on 14th December,
2025.
His conduct during incarceration and parole has been good and he socialized with other co-inmates and helped the other co- inmates in their daily life work.
It is also indicated in the said report that the applicant will reintegrate in the society if released him prematurely.

5. On merits, Mr. Mahapatra, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that even assuming for the sake of argument that the evidence against the appellant may have proved the charge under Section 304B and 498A of the Indian Penal Code, the leverage granted to the Trial Judge for imposing a sentence between seven years and life was required to be informed with sufficient reasons and a sentence for life must be in extreme and rare circumstances.

He further submits that while it may be true that the charge under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code may have been proved, the applicant was inebriated at the time when the incident occurred and was not in his senses.

6. Given the fact that the appellant has served sentence for 17 years and 7 days and in view of the fact that chance of the appeal being heard in near future is very remote although paper books is ready and considering further fact that the appellant's behaviour during incarceration has been good, this Court is inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant.

7. Accordingly, we direct that pending hearing of the appeal, the order of execution of sentence shall remain suspended and the appellant, namely, Tinku @ Md. Asif shall be released on bail on bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of Rs.5,000/- each, to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Asansol, Paschim Bardhaman, subject to the condition that the applicant shall report to the Officer-in-charge, Kulti Police Station twice in a month until further orders and on further condition that he shall not leave the jurisdiction of Kulti Police Station without the express permission in writing of the Trial Judge.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Asansol, Paschim Bardhaman
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. In default of compliance of any of the aforesaid conditions, the bail of the appellant shall stand automatically cancelled and the appellant shall be taken into custody without any further reference to this Court.
9. The application being CRAN 1 of 2025 shall stand disposed of.

It appears from the records that since the paper books in this matter have been prepared and served upon the respective parties, list the appeal in the Monthly Combined List of April, 2026 under the heading "Hearing".
11.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, be given to the parties as expeditiously as possible on compliance of necessary formalities.

(Rajasekhar Mantha, J.) (Ajay Kumar Gupta, J.)
